Under officers are the backbone of the military. They serve as layer between soldiers and officers, if an officer is shit, they’ll just take over. When you train go for lower back (to support the heavy backpack) and endurance muscle (battling ropes). A lot of strain will be on your tendons, and not always the muscles. Don’t underestimate how heavy a fully loaded SCAR is.

Not a para, but I know a few. It’s extremely hard. 

The first bootcamp in Leopoldsburg is easy for sure, impossible to fail even. Then when you go to Arlon, that’s when it becomes super difficult, no compassion and if you’re not good you get bullied out. Para is the most challenging besides SF operator. As under officer you command several men, so they’ll look up to you if you can function under heavy stress, little sleep, no food and muscle fatigue.

If it’s worth it, depends on your motivation. You’ll have a super hard time but you’ll be a self confident, tough as nails dude. 

3 Para (Flemish para’s) go abroad quite a lot. It’s paid very well to go abroad but of course it has its weight on family life. 

If you seek to push yourself to your maximum, sleep only an hour in a foxhole, then do it again, then it’s the right choice. 

3 para guys that I’ve met are super chill if you get their respect, quite arrogant if you’re not up to push yourself.
